key_insight: LoRA factor gradients cannot reveal task-relevant directions normal to the current low-rank manifold, so rank adaptation must assess what is missing—not just what is used.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-guided rank expansion can improve fine-tuning quality while reducing trainable parameter budgets.
method: Optimize existing degrees of freedom using tangent-space information.
Estimate the normal spectrum matrix-free to identify locally optimal rank-expansion directions under a quadratic model.
Use task-induced geometric initialization for the expanded adaptation space.
evidence_signal: Across evaluated language and vision settings, GEAR reports the best average performance; on LLaMA3-8B, average commonsense score rises from 86.61 to 88.45 while trainable parameters fall from 42.0M to 14.4M.
watch_item: The expansion guarantee relies on a local quadratic model, and the abstract does not quantify normal-spectrum estimation overhead.
paper_title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA
